failedAssertions.reason: Step 2 (online_closed day) fails on a new defect: after the first mutation of a date that has never been mutated, the guest channel keeps serving stale availability. The public availability ETag is "<dayVersion>.<settingsVersion>.<flagBits>"; readDayVersion defaults to 1 when rsv_day_versions has no row and the first write inserts version 1 (apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-public-engine.ts:438-454, rsv-setup-crud.ts:111-132), so closing the day leaves the ETag unchanged ("1.68.11"). The Sites page's cached availability body revalidates with If-None-Match and gets 304 (Cache-Control: private, max-age=0), so the guest sees the pre-change 36 time chips while a cache-bypassing fetch returns the correct closed note. Parent reproduced independently on 2026-11-26: create closed special day -> ETag "1.68.11", If-None-Match replay -> 304, fresh fetch -> status closed / 0 slots; delete -> "2.68.11". The same root cause hides the first booking on a never-mutated date from the ETag (staff booking on 2026-11-27 -> ETag still "1.68.11", replay 304), which also breaks VAL-ONLINE-002's 'after any booking... new ETag' clause (not re-tested this round). Everything else in the assertion is fixed: step 3 (closed day) blocks staff booking with the sheet alert + disabled submit, 409 closed_day without override and 201 with a closed_day warning on the explicit override; step 4 (staff_only 4-top) removes public party-4 slots (17 -> 0) while party 2 keeps slots and staff availability still offers party 4; step 5 hides the pacing bucket from Sites and warns the staff channel at submit time (409 pacing_parties_exceeded; 201 + warnings array + 'Booked over the pacing party limit.' toast on the explicit override) - the only step-5 deviation is the persisting round-1 gap that the availability payload still reports available=true / pacingWarning=false for a max_parties-only breach (rsv-day-feed-service.ts:1500-1504 evaluates only maxCovers).
failedAssertions.evidence: evidence/guest-channels-and-crm/r2-app-sheet/step2-sites-stale-availability-defect.txt, step2-stale-cache-evidence.txt, step2-public-p2-online-closed.json, step2-sites-online-closed-p2.png, step1-baseline-public-p2.json; parent verification /tmp/r2-parent-verify (ETag "1.68.11" with the closed day present, If-None-Match -> 304, delete -> "2.68.11")

documentedDeviations.note: Carried forward from round 1: the second conversion attempt with the same hold token answered 410 hold_expired (the contract only requires that it fail).

Carried forward from round 1 and accepted: the contract's literal second step answers 410 hold_expired because the hold token was consumed; the expected 409 slot_unavailable + alternatives was produced by a fresh hold attempt. Not re-opened in round 2.

Carried forward from round 1: the waitlist-off half was verified end to end; the alternatives half was verified at the API payload because the same-day alternatives branch cannot render.

Round 2 was API-level for the guest channel (group r2-backend-rules, curl): the Sites time chips were not driven in a browser, because the round-2 brief scoped the re-test to the fixed operator read and the chips render from the public availability endpoint that was exercised. The UI half passed in round 1 (b1/g14 evidence) and the public availability behavior was re-confirmed here.

The brief's extra phrasing 'a booking on an online_closed day carries a closed-day flag' does not match the implemented shape: the onlineClosed flag lives in the availability payload/day state, not in the booking response. The contract itself only requires operator availability to return slots for D2, which it does.

The operator cancel UI still has no reason input (cancels immediately with a 60 s undo; cancel_reason NULL), so the 'with a reason' wording was satisfied through the API cancel path. Same observation as round 1; no assertion failed on it.
The contract names GET /reservations/manage/calendar.ics while the manage page's own button calls the alias /reservations/manage/ics; both were exercised and both return text/calendar.
